newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures slide on weak banking stocks.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures slide on weak banking stocks.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Wednesday on continued weakness in banking and brokerage stocks on the underlying cash market.
But dealers said the market was still confined to its recent 500-point range and showed no clear trend at the moment.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract lost 340 points to end at 17,710 after hitting a low of 17,670 on light volume of 15,040 lots.

"The reason the Nikkei didn't rally was because of further weakness in the banking and broking sectors. A couple of banks revised down their earnings forecasts," said a dealer with a European futures house.
He said the utilities sector was also hit by concerns the weakening yen would drive up costs of imported raw materials.
Buying of blue chips and export-related shares as the dollar shot to a new high of 126.93 yen failed to push the market back into positive territory.
"Until we break below 17,600 or above 18,200, we're not going anywhere," said the dealer.
A Japanese bank dealer said comments by Japanese officials indicating the Bank of Japan would maintain its easy monetary policy for the time being helped support the market.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 355.6 against its opening 347.0 on volume of 2,285 lots.
Dealers said market turnover was being boosted partly by locals switching to the Taiwan stock futures in the face of the Nikkei market's uninspired performance.
The contract's 10-point discount to the cash index drew traders who were still bullish on the market, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary.

"Sentiment remains positive on the Taiwan contract, although institutional investors with Taiwan equity exposure seem unsure that the rally can continue without some further consolidation taking place," Refco said.
